description: Server-signed, operator-bound Slack Retry action on retryable failure notices with a durable, idempotent Retry operation that creates a recoverable new execution attempt (new Session for root retries, targeted follow-up for thread retries) without touching the failed Turn.

tasks.title: Retry application service core: failure-category allowlist, durable operation store, root-message retry into a new Session
tasks.description: Build the provider-agnostic retry operation surface. Add the authoritative AgentSessionRetryPolicy.IsRetryable exact-match allowlist, defined over the failure-category vocabulary the system actually records (runner-unavailable, runner-lost, report-timeout from server reconciliation; deadline-exceeded, timeout, generation-drain-timeout, unavailable-runtime, runtime-unavailable from runner error kinds; reserved forward-looking rate-limited, probe-timeout, retry-safe; absent/empty/unknown are not retryable) next to the future retry service in Sessions services. Add the agent_retry_operations EF migration (operation id PK, unique idempotency key, unique session+turn, kind, pre-allocated execution identity, Pending→Finished state, recorded result, timestamps) with an AgentRetryOperationStore implementing claim-or-create on the two unique indexes. Implement AgentSessionRetryService.RetryAsync(projectId, sessionId, turnId, idempotencyKey): re-read the target Turn's current failure facts and re-apply the policy (reject no_longer_retryable, creating nothing), decide root vs thread from IsLaunchTurn, pre-allocate execution identity, commit the pending record BEFORE any dispatch, then for root retries rebuild ConnectionLaunchOrigin from the failed Turn's provenance and call IAgentLauncher.LaunchConnectionAsync with a new optional idempotency-key override (agent-retry:{operationId}) so a genuinely new Session with fresh identities is minted, and record the Finished result. The failed Turn is never modified.
acceptanceCriteria: UnitTests cover the classifier matrix pinned to the real recorded vocabulary, never the allowlist's own re-typed tokens: server reconciliation reasons (referencing the AgentJobFailureReasons constants directly) — runner-unavailable, runner-lost, report-timeout retryable, workspace-unavailable not; runner runtime error kinds — deadline-exceeded, timeout, generation-drain-timeout, unavailable-runtime, runtime-unavailable retryable, invalid-input, permission-required, incompatible-runtime, incompatible-execution-configuration, unsupported_execution_configuration, missing-session, runtime-session-missing, conflict, interrupted, turn-failed, manager-credential-expired not; reserved tokens rate-limited, probe-timeout, retry-safe retryable; absent, empty, and unknown values are not; transient-sounding reason text with a permanent category is not retryable; retry-safe with ordinary text is retryable

SpecTests prove persist-before-dispatch: a crash between commit and dispatch leaves a Pending record with its pre-allocated identity, and the dispatch path refuses to run without a committed pending record

SpecTests prove at-most-once: two concurrent RetryAsync calls with the same idempotency key resolve to one operation row and both return the same recorded result (a loser reading while the winner is still Pending reports the accepted-pending record; a later redelivery reports the finished one); a second call for the same (session, turn) with a different key resolves to the existing row's recorded result

SpecTests prove root retry: accepted retry of a launch Turn creates a new Session with the pre-allocated identity, distinct from and independently observable alongside the failed Session, launched through the same launch path as the original
SpecTests prove the failed Turn keeps its original status, failure reason, and failure category unchanged after the retry attempt is created
SpecTests prove no_longer_retryable re-evaluation (target facts superseded) creates no operation row and no execution resources
EF migration applies cleanly with no changes to existing tables; dotnet build and the full Server test suite pass
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Services/AgentSessionRetryPolicy.cs, AgentSessionRetryService, Infrastructure/Data agent_retry_operations migration, AgentRetryOperationStore, plus UnitTests and SpecTests coverage
tasks.notes: Classification is exact ordinal comparison on recorded AgentTurnResult.FailureCategory only; never text heuristics (design Decision 1). The allowlist tokens are pinned to the recorded producer vocabulary (design Decision 1 table): server AgentJobFailureReasons constants and runner RuntimeError kinds (Pi maps deadline-exceeded→timeout and missing-session→runtime-session-missing via mapPiErrorKind; OpenCode kinds pass verbatim via mapOpenCodeErrorKind). The unique (session, turn) index is what makes later re-rendered buttons safe. CLI/Web routes later call this same service unchanged.

tasks.title: Thread retry: explicitly targeted follow-up dispatch in the original Session
tasks.description: Extend AgentSessionRetryService so a failed thread follow-up Turn retries inside the original Session: call IAgentSessionGrain.AcceptFollowupAsync with the failed Turn's input text and durable Slack provenance (same thread root and conversation), idempotency key agent-retry:{operationId} and the pre-minted input id; then dispatch via a new grain method BeginFollowupDispatchForTurnAsync(turnId), implemented as the body of BeginNextFollowupDispatchAsync selecting the given turn instead of the first eligible queued one while keeping the same executing/JobId guards. If the Session is busy the new turn simply stays queued under the ordinary scheduler; the retry never schedules, promotes, or dispatches unrelated queued turns. The operation reaches Finished once the attempt is durably created (follow-up accepted), not when the runner acknowledges.
acceptanceCriteria: Grain/SpecTests prove targeted dispatch: BeginFollowupDispatchForTurnAsync dispatches exactly the given queued turn, keeps the existing executing/JobId guards, and leaves unrelated queued turns queued when a Session with multiple queued turns is retried
SpecTests prove the new follow-up's provenance binds to the same thread root and conversation as the original failed Turn
SpecTests prove a busy (executing) Session accepts the retry turn into the queue without dispatching it or any unrelated turn, and ordinary scheduler order governs onward dispatch

SpecTests prove crash-recovery re-dispatch of the same operation id is idempotent via AcceptFollowupAsync's idempotency key (one accepted turn, one dispatch) and that the operation is recorded Finished once the attempt is durably created
SpecTests prove the failed thread Turn's status, failure reason, and failure category remain unchanged and the attempt carries fresh input/turn identities
Existing follow-up concurrency and dispatch grain specs remain green
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Grains/IAgentSessionGrain.cs and AgentSessionGrain.FollowupDispatch.cs targeted-dispatch method, AgentSessionRetryService thread path, plus grain and SpecTests coverage
tasks.notes: Do NOT force-dispatch past the executing guard (design Decision 7): queueing is the Session's existing answer to a busy session. Keep BeginNextFollowupDispatchAsync behavior unchanged apart from sharing its selection body.

tasks.title: Signed Retry action payload and terminal failure presentation on retryable failures
tasks.description: Render the Retry button. Extract the HMAC-SHA256 sign/verify helpers from SlackTurnControlService into a small shared internal helper (Stop's external behavior, signature, and outcomes untouched) and add a SlackRetryActionPayload mirroring SlackStopActionPayload (v1, action 'retry', Connection/Session/Turn ids, conversation+message+thread identity, operator = session initiator, nonce, five-minute expiry, signature; constant-time compare). Add SlackRetryActionService.CreateRetryActionAsync, suppressing the action when signing material is unavailable. Additively extend SlackTerminalDelivery with sessionId/turnId; make AgentSessionGrain.TryEmitFollowupDeliveryAsync populate failureReason/failureCategory from turn.Result (absent facts degrade to no button). In SlackTerminalDeliveryHandler, when a terminal delivery settles a failed Turn with a retryable recorded category (via the single AgentSessionRetryPolicy), enqueue an explicit failure notice through SlackStatusProjection.EnqueueTerminalAsync (promoting the replaceable progress row in place) with blocks carrying the Retry action; non-retryable, absent-category, non-failure, and Manager-project deliveries keep exactly today's reaction-only finalization.
acceptanceCriteria: SpecTests prove a retryable failed Turn's terminal notice renders a Retry action button whose action value carries an expiry no more than five minutes after creation, while non-retryable, absent-category, completed/cancelled, and Manager DM presentations render no Retry action and stay byte-for-byte on the current text/reaction presentation

UnitTests cover the payload sign/verify matrix: tampered values, absent nonce/version/action name/signature are rejected; verification uses FixedTimeEquals; unavailable signing material suppresses the action and keeps the plain notice

SpecTests prove presentation consumes the single AgentSessionRetryPolicy (no Slack-local copy) and that a follow-up terminal event now carries failureCategory from turn.Result while a null-category event still yields no button
The existing SlackTurnControlInteractionSpecs (Stop behavior) pass unchanged, pinning that the signing-helper extraction is internal-only
SlackTerminalDelivery validation and existing terminal/outbox delivery specs remain green with the additive fields
dotnet build and the full Server test suite pass
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Slack/Services/SlackRetryActionService.cs (creation side) and shared signing helper, Infrastructure/Slack SlackTerminalDelivery + SlackTerminalDeliveryHandler changes, AgentSessionGrain.SlackDelivery failure-fact population, plus UnitTests and SpecTests coverage
tasks.notes: Operator binding is the session initiator (initial launch provenance member), the same binding Stop uses. Until the route task lands, a click on the rendered button is harmlessly rejected as unsupported by the existing route. The production fact source for follow-up failure categories lands in T-007 (runner-side); T-003's specs inject categories to pin the server-side forwarding and degradation independently.

tasks.title: Runner reports the runtime error kind as failureCategory on terminal follow-up activity events
tasks.description: Close the producer-side gap that keeps thread-retry presentation unreachable in production. Today the runner's follow-up terminal events carry only failureReason (packages/runner/src/server/followup-handler.ts recordFollowupActivity sets failureCategory only for expired manager credentials, as unknown), and follow-up turns never pass through AgentJobGrain, so no server-side reconciliation supplies a category either — every ordinary thread failure settles with a null category and can never render a Retry button. When a follow-up turn fails with a runtime error kind, recordFollowupActivity MUST emit that kind as failureCategory on the terminal session.activity payload, applying the same kind→category mapping the AgentJob path applies (mapOpenCodeErrorKind / mapPiErrorKind semantics — Pi deadline-exceeded reports timeout and missing-session reports runtime-session-missing; OpenCode kinds report verbatim): extract or reuse the mapping from runtime/agent-job-turn.ts rather than duplicating it. Failures without a recoverable error kind (observer flush errors, rejected calls, thrown exceptions) keep omitting failureCategory, and expired manager credentials keep recording unknown; both degrade to no button. The field is additive on the event payload — runners predating it remain valid and the Server classifies absent categories as not retryable. No Server change is required: AgentSessionGrain.ResolveFollowupTurnResult already reads failureCategory from the payload, and T-003 forwards turn.Result facts into the follow-up delivery envelope.
acceptanceCriteria: Runner tests prove a failed follow-up whose runtime result carries an error kind (for example unavailable-runtime or deadline-exceeded from OpenCode, deadline-exceeded from Pi) records that mapped kind as failureCategory on the terminal session.activity event alongside failureReason

Runner tests prove the mapping matches the AgentJob path exactly (Pi deadline-exceeded → timeout, missing-session → runtime-session-missing, OpenCode kinds verbatim) via a shared mapping helper, not a copied table
Runner tests prove failures without a recoverable error kind omit failureCategory and expired manager credentials keep recording unknown
The terminal event shape stays otherwise unchanged (id, activity, status, failureReason, message/output, source, operationId fields as today) and existing runner follow-up-handler tests remain green
npm test in packages/runner passes
tasks.output: packages/runner/src/server/followup-handler.ts failure-category reporting (kind→category mapping shared with runtime/agent-job-turn.ts), plus runner test coverage
tasks.notes: Producer side of the thread-retry fact chain: runner emits failureCategory → AgentSessionGrain.ResolveFollowupTurnResult stores it on turn.Result → T-003's TryEmitFollowupDeliveryAsync forwards it → presentation classifies it. Independent of the Server tasks (different package) and composes with T-003 by value; the absent ⇒ no-button degradation stays as the safety net for old runners and unknown failures, not as the permanent behavior.

tasks.title: Retry interaction route dispatch, acceptance revalidation, and Slack feedback
tasks.description: Wire the click. Extend SlackInteractionRoutes to dispatch by action id while keeping its envelope (operator auth, adapter lease validation, Connection resolution, disabled-Connection rejection, outbox UserAction reply with the identity-stable ActionDispatchRef): mohist_stop_turn stays on SlackTurnControlService unchanged; new mohist_retry_turn goes to SlackRetryActionService.HandleAsync. HandleAsync performs, in order: signature verify → five-minute expiry → context match (Connection id, team id, conversation id) → exact operator binding → current permission (operator still Connection Owner or session initiator, and the Connection's current access policy does not deny the operator in that conversation, reusing the ingress decider's policy read) → hand off to AgentSessionRetryService with idempotencyKey = action nonce, which re-checks target retryability and returns the recorded operation result. Every rejection returns an explicit state plus user-facing text through the outbox reply; an accepted click posts attempt-accepted feedback; the route implements no second retry command grammar.
acceptanceCriteria: SpecTests prove each rejection outcome creates no execution resources and returns explicit text: tampered/invalid action, expired, stale context (Connection/team/conversation mismatch), different Slack member, operator no longer Owner/initiator or denied by current access policy, disabled Connection, and no-longer-retryable target

SpecTests prove an accepted Retry click passes the same adapter lease validation and Connection resolution as a Stop click, dispatches to AgentSessionRetryService (the same service a CLI/Web retry uses), and Slack receives attempt-accepted feedback through the outbox user-action reply

SpecTests prove redelivery/replay of the same click updates the same identity-stable reply (no duplicate feedback) and resolves to the same recorded operation result with no second attempt (including a replay arriving while the operation is still Pending, which reports the accepted-pending record)
SpecTests prove Stop behavior (signature, five-minute lifetime, revalidation, outcome states, replay handling) is unchanged before and after the Retry action id exists on the same route
The route performs no retry decision logic itself — all retry semantics flow through AgentSessionRetryService
dotnet build and the full Server test suite pass
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Api/SlackInteractionRoutes.cs action-id dispatch, Slack/Services/SlackRetryActionService.cs HandleAsync acceptance path, plus SpecTests coverage (new SlackRetryInteractionSpecs alongside SlackTurnControlInteractionSpecs)
tasks.notes: Click idempotency lives in the operation receipt (unique indexes), NOT in SlackProviderInboxStore — the inbox keeps owning only raw Slack message ingress. Concurrent/redelivered clicks converge on the recorded result from T-001.

tasks.title: AgentRetryObligationWorker: restart recovery of pending Retry operations and bounded cleanup
tasks.description: Add an AgentRetryObligationWorker BackgroundService following the SlackAgentAppBindingObligationWorker pattern (~1-minute interval, scope per pass, catch-all logging, never throws). Each pass resumes every Pending agent_retry_operations row by re-running the same idempotent dispatch through AgentSessionRetryService (coordinator replay for root retries, AcceptFollowupAsync idempotency + targeted dispatch for thread retries) — no original click, lease, or interaction needed — and the construction is idempotent so no second attempt can result. The same pass deletes Finished rows past a 24-hour retention window and never deletes Pending rows. Register the worker in MohistServiceRegistration.
acceptanceCriteria: SpecTests prove restart recovery: a committed-but-Pending row (including a crash between commit and dispatch) is resumed by the worker, targets the pre-allocated execution identity recorded on the row, and results in exactly one new attempt without the original click lease
SpecTests prove Finished rows past the retention window are deleted and Pending rows are never removed while the cleanup runs (use an injectable TimeProvider)
SpecTests prove the worker pass is exception-safe: a failing row is retried on the next pass without stopping the loop or other rows
SpecTests prove resumed dispatch of an already-completed operation is a no-op returning the recorded result (no second attempt after adapter failover or redelivery)
The worker is registered in hosting DI and starts/stops cleanly with the Server; dotnet build and the full Server test suite pass
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Sessions/Services/AgentRetryObligationWorker.cs (or Agent/Services per placement convention), DI registration, plus SpecTests recovery/cleanup coverage
tasks.notes: Recovery reuses the same idempotent pipelines as the live click path — no separate recovery code path. Retention window 24 h per design open question (flag shorter windows in review, do not block).
